setting: A small café in Madrid at mid-morning, not busy. The tutor is the barista; the learner has just walked up to the counter and is buying drinks for themselves and maybe a friend waiting at a table.

goal.en: Say hello back and order a drink.

expect.meaning: greets and orders a coffee or another drink
match: buenos días, un café con leche, por favor

goal.en: Say what drink you would like.

expect.meaning: says they want a coffee or another drink

goal.en: Say how many you want: one is enough.
goal.ko: 몇 잔인지 말하세요. 한 잔이면 돼요.

goal.en: Say that's all and ask how much it is.

expect.meaning: says no, nothing else, without asking the price

goal.en: Hand over the money and thank them.

expect.meaning: did not catch the price and asks again

goal.en: Say goodbye.

gloss.en: Hi, good morning! What can I get you?
Hi. What do you want?
Good morning! Tell me, what would you like?
Would you like a coffee or a tea?

menu.text: Tenemos café, té y zumo de naranja.

gloss.en: We have coffee, tea and orange juice.
There's coffee, tea or juice.
Very good. How many? One or two?
gloss.ko: 좋아요. 몇 잔요? 한 잔, 두 잔?

gloss.en: Do you want one or two?
gloss.ko: 한 잔 드려요, 두 잔 드려요?

gloss.en: Perfect. Anything else?
Do you want anything else?
That's two euros fifty.

price-easy.text: Son dos euros y cincuenta céntimos.

gloss.en: It's two euros and fifty cents.

bye.text: Aquí tienes. ¡Que tengas un buen día!

gloss.en: Here you go. Have a nice day!
Thank you! See you!

setting: A busy street outside Atocha train station in Madrid, early afternoon. The learner has stopped a friendly local passer-by to ask the way to the metro.

goal.en: Say sorry for stopping them and ask where the subway is.
goal.ko: 실례한다고 하고 지하철이 어디 있는지 물어보세요.

match: sí, ¿dónde está el metro, por favor?
hola, ¿dónde está la estación de metro?

expect.meaning: asks whether there is a metro nearby

goal.en: It was too fast. Ask them to say it again, slowly.
goal.ko: 너무 빨랐어요. 천천히 다시 말해 달라고 하세요.

expect.meaning: asks them to repeat or speak slowly

goal.en: Say OK, and ask if there is a chemist's around here too.
goal.ko: 알았다고 하고, 이 근처에 약국도 있는지 물어보세요.

expect.meaning: asks if there is a pharmacy nearby

goal.en: Thank them for their help and say goodbye.

gloss.en: Yes? Hi. Are you looking for something?
Hi. Do you need help?

dir.text: Está cerca. Todo recto y luego la segunda a la derecha.

gloss.en: It's close. Straight on and then the second on the right.
gloss.ko: 가까워요. 쭉 가다가 두 번째 길에서 오른쪽이요.

dir-easy.text: Todo recto. Luego, a la derecha.

gloss.en: Straight on. Then, to the right.

slow.text: Claro. Todo... recto. Y luego... a la derecha. Cinco minutos.

gloss.en: Sure. Straight... on. And then... right. Five minutes.

slow-easy.text: Vas recto y luego a la derecha.

gloss.en: You go straight and then right.
That's it! It's very easy. Anything else?
gloss.ko: 맞아요! 아주 쉬워요. 또 필요한 거 있어요?

gloss.en: Do you need anything else?

pharmacy.text: Sí, hay una al lado del metro.

gloss.en: Yes, there's one next to the metro.

pharmacy-easy.text: Sí, está al lado del metro.

gloss.en: Yes, it's next to the metro.
OK. Well, all the best!
OK. Have a good day!
You're welcome! Bye!

setting: A small souvenir shop in the old town of Seville, late morning. The tutor is the shop assistant. The learner wants a postcard and notices a hand fan.

goal.en: Say what you would like to buy: a postcard.
Point at the thing next to the postcards and ask what it is.
goal.ko: 엽서 옆에 있는 물건을 가리키며 뭔지 물어보세요.

expect.meaning: already knows and checks it is a fan

goal.en: Answer: do you like it?
Ask how much the fan is.

expect.meaning: asks the total or the price of the postcards

goal.en: Say you'll take the fan and one postcard.
goal.ko: 부채와 엽서 한 장을 사겠다고 하세요.

expect.meaning: asks for the fan and a postcard
match: el abanico y una postal, por favor
el abanico y la postal, por favor

goal.en: Answer whether you need a bag.

gloss.en: Hello. Are you looking for something?
Hi. Do you need something?

cards.text: Claro, las postales están aquí. Y esto también es muy típico.

gloss.en: Sure, the postcards are here. And this is very typical too.
gloss.ko: 그럼요, 엽서는 여기 있어요. 그리고 이것도 아주 전통적인 거예요.

gloss.en: The postcards are here.

browse.text: Vale, tranquilo. Mira, aquí hay postales y esto, muy típico.

gloss.en: OK, no problem. Look, here are postcards and this, very typical.
gloss.ko: 네, 천천히 보세요. 여기 엽서가 있고, 이건 아주 전통적인 거예요.

fan.text: Es un abanico, para el calor. ¿Te gusta?

gloss.en: It's a hand fan, for the heat. Do you like it?
gloss.ko: 부채예요, 더울 때 써요. 마음에 들어요?

gloss.en: It's a fan. Do you like it?

fan-yes.text: ¡Sí, un abanico! Muy típico de Sevilla. ¿Te gusta?

gloss.en: Yes, a fan! Very typical of Seville. Do you like it?
gloss.ko: 네, 부채예요! 세비야 전통이에요. 마음에 들어요?

nice.text: Es precioso, ¿verdad? Y no es caro.

gloss.en: It's lovely, isn't it? And it isn't expensive.
It's pretty. It isn't expensive.
OK. There are other colours, look.
There are other colours too.

price.text: El abanico, ocho euros. La postal, un euro.

gloss.en: The fan, eight euros. The postcard, one euro.
The fan costs eight euros.
Very good. Do you want a bag?
Do you need a bag?

end.text: Perfecto. Son nueve euros. ¡Gracias, hasta luego!

gloss.en: Perfect. That's nine euros. Thanks, see you!

setting: The front desk of a small family-run hotel in Granada, early evening. The tutor is the receptionist and speaks politely (usted). The learner has a booking for two nights.

goal.en: Greet the receptionist and say you have a booking.

match: tengo una reserva para dos noches

goal.en: Tell the receptionist your name.
Hand it over and say that it is yours.

expect.meaning: hands it over saying it is their passport
match: sí, aquí tiene. es mi pasaporte

goal.en: Ask what time breakfast is.

match: perdón, ¿a qué hora es el desayuno?

expect.meaning: did not catch the room number

goal.en: Say OK and ask where the lift is.
goal.ko: 알았다고 하고 엘리베이터가 어디 있는지 물어보세요.

goal.en: Thank the receptionist for everything.

expect.meaning: thanks for everything or for the help

gloss.en: Good evening, welcome. Do you have a booking?
Do you have a booking?
Perfect. What's your name?
Your name, please?

passport.text: Sí, aquí está. Dos noches. ¿Su pasaporte, por favor?

gloss.en: Yes, here it is. Two nights. Your passport, please?
The passport, please?

room.text: Gracias. Su habitación es la doce.

gloss.en: Thank you. Your room is number twelve.
It's room number twelve.

breakfast.text: De siete a diez, en el comedor.

gloss.en: From seven to ten, in the dining room.

breakfast-easy.text: El desayuno es de siete a diez.

gloss.en: Breakfast is from seven to ten.

lift.text: Allí, a la derecha. Es la segunda planta.

gloss.en: Over there, on the right. It's the second floor.

lift-easy.text: El ascensor está allí, a la derecha.

gloss.en: The lift is over there, on the right.
You're welcome. Good night!

setting: A language-exchange meetup in a café in Madrid, early evening. The tutor is Lucía, a friendly Spanish woman from Valencia, and starts the chat. Informal (tú).

goal.en: Greet her and say your name.
Say where you are from.
Say what your job is.

expect.meaning: says they work, without the job name

goal.en: Say where you work.
Now ask her the same question.

expect.meaning: asks a yes/no question about her job

goal.en: Say goodbye until later.

gloss.en: Hi! I'm Lucía. What's your name?
My name is Lucía. And you?
Nice to meet you. And where are you from?
Are you from Korea? From China?

job.text: ¡Qué bien! Yo soy de Valencia. ¿Y tú estudias o trabajas?

gloss.en: Great! I'm from Valencia. And do you study or work?
gloss.ko: 좋다! 나는 발렌시아 출신이야. 너는 공부해, 일해?

gloss.en: Do you work? What's your job?
How interesting! And where do you work?
Do you work in an office?
Great! That's interesting.
Very good.

lucia.text: Yo soy estudiante. Estudio Medicina. Bueno, empieza la clase.

gloss.en: I'm a student. I study medicine. Well, the class is starting.
gloss.ko: 나는 학생이야. 의학 공부해. 자, 수업 시작한다.

gloss.en: I'm a student. Now we have class.
See you later!

setting: A café in Salamanca in the afternoon. The tutor is a Spanish friend looking at a family photo on the learner's phone: the learner's sister and a dog. Informal (tú).

goal.en: Thank them and say she is your sister.
Say you have a brother too.

match: tengo un hermano y una hermana

goal.en: Say how old you are.
Say yes, it's your dog.

match: sí, es mi perro. se llama toto
es mi perro, se llama toto

expect.meaning: says it belongs to the sister
match: no, es el perro de mi hermana

goal.en: Say whether you like dogs.

photo.text: ¡Qué foto tan bonita! ¿Quién es esta chica?

gloss.en: What a lovely photo! Who is this girl?
Who is it? Your sister?
She's very pretty. Do you have more brothers or sisters?
Do you have brothers or sisters?

age.text: Es muy joven. ¿Y tú cuántos años tienes?

gloss.en: She's very young. And how old are you?
How old are you?
OK. And this dog? Is it yours?
Is it your dog?
How lovely! Do you like dogs?
Do you like animals?

end-yes.text: ¡A mí también! Tu familia es muy simpática.

gloss.en: Me too! Your family is really nice.
gloss.ko: 나도! 너희 가족 정말 좋아 보인다.

gloss.en: No? But this dog is very lovely!
gloss.ko: 아니야? 그래도 이 강아지는 정말 예쁘다!

setting: A busy tapas bar in Madrid in the evening. The tutor is a new Spanish friend sharing a drink with the learner and suggesting what to order. Informal (tú).

goal.en: Say yes, good idea.
You don't know that word. Say you don't understand it.

expect.meaning: says they don't understand the word

goal.en: Tell your friend honestly that you don't like it.

match: no, no me gusta el pulpo

goal.en: Say what you want to eat.

expect.meaning: says what they want to eat

goal.en: Ask your friend to get you a drink.

gloss.en: Hey, are you hungry? Shall we order some tapas?
Shall we eat something? Yes?

pulpo.text: Mira, aquí tienen pulpo a la gallega. ¿Te gusta el pulpo?

gloss.en: Look, they have Galician-style octopus here. Do you like octopus?
gloss.ko: 봐, 여기 갈리시아식 문어 있어. 문어 좋아해?

gloss.en: Do you like octopus?

octopus.text: Es un animal del mar. Tiene ocho patas. ¿Te gusta?

gloss.en: It's a sea animal. It has eight legs. Do you like it?
gloss.ko: 바다 동물이야. 다리가 여덟 개야. 좋아해?

octopus-easy.text: Es un animal del mar. ¿Te gusta?

gloss.en: It's a sea animal. Do you like it?

dislike.text: ¿No? ¡Vale, no pasa nada! ¿Y qué quieres comer?

gloss.en: No? OK, no problem! So what do you want to eat?
gloss.ko: 아니야? 괜찮아! 그럼 뭐 먹고 싶어?

like.text: ¡Genial! Lo pedimos. ¿Y qué más quieres comer?

gloss.en: Great! We'll order it. And what else do you want to eat?
gloss.ko: 좋아! 그거 시키자. 또 뭐 먹고 싶어?

gloss.en: Do you want omelette or potatoes?

drink.text: ¡Buena idea! Voy a la barra. ¿Qué quieres beber?

gloss.en: Good idea! I'm going to the bar. What do you want to drink?
gloss.ko: 좋은 생각! 바에 갔다 올게. 뭐 마실래?

gloss.en: Do you want water or a small beer?

cana.text: Una caña es una cerveza pequeña.

gloss.en: A 'caña' is a small beer.
OK! Back in a moment.

setting: The first meeting of a weekend international club in a community centre in Madrid (cooking, football, language exchange). The tutor is a friendly club member. Informal (tú); speaks a bit fast at one point.

goal.en: Say yes, it's your first time, and say your name.

expect.meaning: says yes and gives their name
match: sí, soy nuevo. me llamo ji-woo
sí, soy nueva. me llamo ji-woo

goal.en: Say whether you cook.
Say no, you don't play football.
Say which languages you speak.

match: hablo coreano y un poco de inglés
coreano, y un poco de español

goal.en: Say yes, you study it.

match: sí, estudio español por la tarde

goal.en: That was fast. Ask them to repeat it more slowly.
goal.ko: 너무 빨랐어요. 더 천천히 다시 말해 달라고 하세요.

expect.meaning: asks to repeat or slow down
match: perdón, ¿puede hablar más despacio, por favor?

goal.en: Say yes, you would like to go.

match: lo siento, el jueves no puedo

gloss.en: Hi! Welcome to the club. Are you new?
gloss.ko: 안녕! 클럽에 온 걸 환영해. 처음이야?

gloss.en: First time here?
Nice to meet you. Hey, do you cook?
Do you like cooking?
Great! And do you play football?

cook-no.text: No pasa nada, aquí aprendes. ¿Y juegas al fútbol?

gloss.en: No problem, you'll learn here. And do you play football?
gloss.ko: 괜찮아, 여기서 배우면 돼. 축구는 해?

gloss.en: Do you like football?
OK. And what languages do you speak?
Do you speak English?
Great! And do you study Spanish?
And do you study Spanish here?

fast.text: ¡Genial! Los jueves tenemos intercambio de idiomas en el bar de la esquina a las ocho.

gloss.en: Great! On Thursdays we have a language exchange at the bar on the corner at eight.
gloss.ko: 좋아! 목요일마다 모퉁이 바에서 8시에 언어 교환 해.

fast-easy.text: Es el jueves, a las ocho.

gloss.en: It's on Thursday, at eight.

slower.text: Claro. Los jueves... a las ocho... hablamos idiomas.

gloss.en: Sure. On Thursdays... at eight... we speak languages.
Do you want to come?
Are you coming on Thursday?
Great! See you on Thursday!
No problem. Another day!

setting: A short phone call at 8:45 on a weekday morning. The tutor is Marta, a friendly colleague at an office in Madrid, calling to see where the learner is and to plan lunch. Informal (tú).

goal.en: Say good morning and say where you are now: on the subway.
goal.ko: 아침 인사를 하고 지금 지하철 안이라고 하세요.

match: buenos días, estoy en el metro

goal.en: Say what time you get up.
Say what time you will arrive.
Agree to have lunch at one.

match: a la una no, a las dos

goal.en: Say see you later.

expect.meaning: says see you later or soon

gloss.en: Good morning! How are you? Where are you?
Hi. Where are you? At home?
Good, good. But where are you now?

wake.text: Ah, vale. Oye, ¿a qué hora te levantas normalmente?

gloss.en: Ah, OK. Hey, what time do you usually get up?
gloss.ko: 아, 그렇구나. 보통 몇 시에 일어나?

wake-easy.text: ¿Te levantas a las siete? ¿A las ocho?

gloss.en: Do you get up at seven? At eight?

arrive.text: Yo, a las siete. ¿Y hoy a qué hora llegas a la oficina?

gloss.en: Me, at seven. And what time do you get to the office today?
gloss.ko: 나는 7시. 오늘은 사무실에 몇 시에 와?

gloss.en: Do you arrive at nine?
Perfect. Shall we have lunch together at one?
Shall we eat at one?
Great! See you later, then.
OK. See you later.
See you soon!

setting: A small square in a residential neighbourhood of Valencia, on a Saturday morning. The tutor is a friendly neighbour who has seen the learner in the street a few times. Informal (tú).

goal.en: Greet them and say yes, you live on this street.
goal.ko: 인사하고, 네, 이 길에 산다고 하세요.

goal.en: Say whether you like the neighbourhood.

match: no sé, es nuevo para mí

goal.en: Ask if there is a place to buy food around here.
goal.ko: 이 근처에 장 볼 가게가 있는지 물어보세요.

expect.meaning: asks if there is a shop nearby

goal.en: Say sorry, you can't: you have a lesson now.
goal.ko: 미안하지만 못 간다고, 지금 수업이 있다고 하세요.

expect.meaning: cannot come, has something to do

goal.en: Thank them for the help and say goodbye.

match: gracias por la ayuda, hasta luego

gloss.en: Hi, good morning! Do you live around here?
Do you live on this street?
Oh, we're neighbours! Do you like the neighbourhood?
gloss.ko: 아, 우리 이웃이네요! 동네 마음에 들어요?

gloss.en: The neighbourhood, do you like it? Yes?

need.text: Oye, ¿necesitas algo? Yo vivo aquí al lado.

gloss.en: Hey, do you need anything? I live right next door.
gloss.ko: 혹시 필요한 거 있어요? 저 바로 옆에 살아요.

gloss.en: Are you looking for a shop?

super.text: Sí, hay uno en la esquina, y una farmacia al lado.

gloss.en: Yes, there's one on the corner, and a pharmacy next to it.
gloss.ko: 네, 모퉁이에 하나 있고 그 옆에 약국도 있어요.

super-easy.text: Sí, está allí, en la esquina.

gloss.en: Yes, it's there, on the corner.

ok.text: Vale. Si necesitas algo, aquí estoy.

gloss.en: OK. If you need anything, I'm here.

market.text: Yo voy al mercado ahora. ¿Vienes conmigo?

gloss.en: I'm going to the market now. Are you coming with me?
gloss.ko: 저 지금 시장 가는데, 같이 갈래요?

gloss.en: Will you come with me to the market?
OK, another day. See you!
OK, another day. Bye!
Great! Let's go, it's just round the corner.
You're welcome, neighbour! Bye!

setting: An outdoor fruit stall at the Saturday market in Valencia, mid-morning. The tutor is Carmen, the stall owner, cheerful and quick, polite but warm (usted).

goal.en: Greet her and ask how much the strawberries are.

expect.meaning: asks the price of the strawberries

goal.en: Ask for one kilo.

match: un kilo de fresas, por favor

expect.meaning: says they want some without a quantity

goal.en: Say how many kilos you want.
Ask how much the oranges are too.
Say yes, one kilo of oranges too.

expect.meaning: asks for a kilo of oranges
match: un kilo de naranjas, por favor
vale, un kilo de naranjas, por favor

goal.en: Pay and thank her.

expect.meaning: asks her to repeat the total

gloss.en: Good morning! What can I get you today?
Good morning. What would you like?

price.text: Las fresas, a tres euros el kilo.

gloss.en: The strawberries, three euros a kilo.

price-easy.text: Un kilo de fresas cuesta tres euros.

gloss.en: A kilo of strawberries costs three euros.

show.text: Mire, hay fresas, naranjas y plátanos. Todo muy bueno.

gloss.en: Look, there are strawberries, oranges and bananas. All very good.
gloss.ko: 보세요, 딸기, 오렌지, 바나나가 있어요. 다 좋아요.

gloss.en: There are strawberries and oranges. What would you like?
Very good. How many kilos do you want?
Do you want one or two kilos?
Here you are. Anything else?
Would you like anything else?

oranges.text: Las naranjas, a dos euros el kilo. ¿Le pongo un kilo?

gloss.en: The oranges, two euros a kilo. Shall I give you a kilo?

oranges-easy.text: Las naranjas cuestan dos euros. ¿Quiere un kilo?

gloss.en: The oranges cost two euros. Do you want a kilo?

total.text: Pues son cinco euros en total.

gloss.en: So that's five euros in total.
It's five euros.
It's five euros in total.
Thank you! All the best!

setting: A small neighbourhood bakery in Barcelona at 8 a.m. The tutor is Jordi, the baker, friendly and polite (usted). There are croissants, a bread loaf and a pastry the learner doesn't know (an ensaimada).

goal.en: Greet him and ask for a loaf of bread.

match: una barra de pan, por favor
buenos días, una barra, por favor

goal.en: Point at a pastry you don't know and ask what it is.
Say you'd like to try it.
Say how many: two.
Ask how much it is in total.
Pay and say goodbye.

gloss.en: Good morning. What will it be?
Hello. What would you like today?
Very good, one baguette. Anything else?
gloss.ko: 좋아요, 바게트 하나요. 더 필요한 거 있어요?

gloss.en: Would you like anything else?
We have bread, croissants and ensaimadas.
There's bread and croissants.

ensaimada.text: Es una ensaimada, un dulce de Mallorca. Está muy rica.

gloss.en: It's an ensaimada, a sweet pastry from Mallorca. It's very tasty.
gloss.ko: 엔사이마다예요, 마요르카 단 빵이에요. 아주 맛있어요.

ensaimada-easy.text: Es un dulce. Está muy rico.

gloss.en: It's a sweet. It's very tasty.
How many would you like?
Do you want one or two?
That's three euros twenty.

total-easy.text: Son tres euros y veinte céntimos.

gloss.en: It's three euros and twenty cents.
Thank you. Have a good day!

setting: A small casual restaurant in Seville at 2 p.m. offering a 'menú del día'. The tutor is the server, quick and friendly, using tú as is common in casual Spanish restaurants.

goal.en: Say yes, a table for one.
Ask for water.

match: una botella de agua, por favor
un zumo de naranja, por favor

goal.en: Answer: still water, please.
Say which one you'd like.
Say that's all and ask how much it is.
Say OK and thank the server.

gloss.en: Hi! Here for lunch? Sit wherever you like.
Hi. Are you eating here?
Very good. What do you want to drink?
Do you want water or a soft drink?
Sparkling or still?
Normal water or sparkling?

food.text: Vale. Y de primero hay sopa o ensalada.

gloss.en: OK. And for the first course there's soup or salad.
gloss.ko: 네. 첫 요리는 수프나 샐러드가 있어요.

gloss.en: Soup or salad?
Very good. Anything else?
Do you want anything else?

bill.text: Es el menú del día: doce euros.

gloss.en: It's the set lunch: twelve euros.
It's twelve euros.
Sure, I'll bring you bread now.
Thank you! Enjoy your meal!

setting: A bus stop on a main avenue in Málaga, late afternoon. The tutor is Rosa, an older woman also waiting, kind and chatty (uses tú with a young person, as is common).

goal.en: Agree, then ask where the bus to the beach is.
goal.ko: 맞다고 하고 해변 가는 버스가 어디 있는지 물어보세요.

expect.meaning: asks where the beach bus is
match: sí. perdón, ¿dónde está el autobús a la playa?

where.text: ¿Qué quieres comer? Hay un japonés y un italiano aquí cerca.

gloss.en: What do you want to eat? There's a Japanese place and an Italian nearby.
gloss.ko: 뭐 먹고 싶어? 근처에 일식집이랑 이탈리아 식당 있어.

gloss.en: Japanese or Italian?

end.text: ¡Perfecto! Pues a la una y media. ¡A trabajar!

gloss.en: Perfect! So at half past one. Back to work!

setting: A Renfe ticket machine at a Cercanías station in Madrid, morning rush. The learner can't make the machine work. The tutor is a station staff member in uniform, polite (usted) and helpful.

goal.en: Say you don't understand the machine and ask for help.
goal.ko: 기계를 잘 모르겠다고 하고 도와 달라고 하세요.

expect.meaning: says they don't understand the machine

goal.en: Ask her to speak more slowly.

expect.meaning: asks to slow down or repeat

goal.en: Say you want to go to Alcalá.

expect.meaning: says where they want to go
match: quiero ir a alcalá de henares
quiero ir a alcalá, por favor

goal.en: You don't understand why. Ask what the card is for.
goal.ko: 왜인지 모르겠어요. 카드를 왜 넣는지 물어보세요.

goal.en: Say OK and do it.
Thank her for her help.

gloss.en: Good morning. Do you have a problem?
Do you need help?

explain.text: A ver. Primero, pulse aquí y elija el destino.

gloss.en: Let's see. First, press here and choose the destination.
gloss.ko: 어디 봐요. 먼저 여기 누르고 목적지를 고르세요.

gloss.en: Press this button, here.
Sure. Press... here. See? This button.
gloss.ko: 그럼요. 여기를… 누르세요. 보여요? 이 버튼이요.

gloss.en: Very good. Where are you going?
Where do you want to go?

card.text: Vale, Alcalá. Ahora meta la tarjeta aquí.

gloss.en: OK, Alcalá. Now put the card in here.
gloss.ko: 네, 알칼라요. 이제 카드를 여기 넣으세요.

gloss.en: Put the card in here, like this.

card-why.text: Para pagar. Meta la tarjeta del banco aquí.

gloss.en: To pay. Put your bank card in here.
Done! Here's the ticket.
This is your ticket.
You're welcome. Have a good trip!

setting: The corridor of a language school in Cádiz, just after the evening class. The tutor is Marco, an Italian classmate who also studies Spanish, cheerful (tú).

goal.en: Say you're going home now.
Say where you are staying now.

match: sí, estoy en una residencia cerca
estoy en un piso en el centro

expect.meaning: says it is close or far

goal.en: Say you're not sure and ask him.

match: sí, el jueves a las seis

goal.en: Say yes, it's yours, and thank him.
goal.ko: 네, 내 거라고 하고 고맙다고 하세요.

goal.en: Say goodbye until Thursday.

hello.text: ¡Por fin! ¡Qué clase tan larga! ¿Adónde vas ahora?

gloss.en: Finally! What a long class! Where are you going now?
gloss.ko: 드디어! 수업 정말 길다! 이제 어디 가?

gloss.en: Are you going home now?
Ah, OK. And where are you living? Close by?
Is your home close?

next.text: Oye, ¿cuándo es la próxima clase? ¿El jueves?

gloss.en: Hey, when is the next class? Thursday?
Is the class on Thursday?

thursday.text: Sí, el jueves a las seis.

gloss.en: Yes, Thursday at six.

thursday-easy.text: Es el jueves a las seis.

gloss.en: It's on Thursday at six.
OK. Oh, is this notebook yours?
gloss.ko: 알았어. 아, 이 공책 네 거야?

gloss.en: Is this notebook yours?
You're welcome! See you on Thursday!
OK, see you!
